# Authentication

The Gorgias API supports two authentication methods:

  1. 🔐 Private app → API key
  2. 👥 Public app → OAuth2

Using OAuth2 is mandatory for public apps.

For testing purposes, you can perform requests directly from the API Reference using your API keys.

  1. Go to any endpoint (e.g: "Retrieve your account")
  2. Use your email (username) and your API key

Access Tokens (API Keys)

# Access Tokens (API Keys)

> ### 👉
> 
> Please remember that the API key authentication method can be used only for private apps. If you plan to build a public app you have to use OAuth2.

Each access token (or API key) is tied to a specific user and has the same permissions as the user that holds them. Requests made with an access token will act on behalf of a user and will have access to the resources their permissions allow. As an admin, you can easily generate and revoke your access token in the settings of your account.

Example: If you use an Access Token for a user with an Observer Agent role, then you can only do the things that an Observer agent can. Learn more about roleshere.

How do I get my API key?

  1. Log in to your Gorgias account
  2. Navigate to Settings → REST API
  3. Click the Create API key button

Once you have your credentials, you can start performing requests directly from the API documentation .

Request example

[Button: cURL]
    
    `curl --request GET \
      --url https://your-customer-account.gorgias.com/api/account \
      --header 'Authorization: Basic base64encode(USERNAME:API_KEY)'`

> ### 👉
> 
> Since we're using HTTP Basic Authentication, the `USERNAME:API_KEY` pair has to be a base64 encoded string. Note the `:` between the `USERNAME` and `API_KEY` is a separator used to differentiate between the username and the password.

# Access your Gorgias REST API credentials Updated 5 months ago

The Gorgias REST API lets you read and write data in your helpdesk programmatically. To authenticate API requests, Gorgias uses HTTP Basic Authentication with three pieces of information: your base API URL, your email address, and an API key. You can find and manage all three from the REST API settings page in your helpdesk.

Note: API keys are tied to your individual account, not to the helpdesk as a whole.

For full API documentation, visit the Gorgias Developer Documentation.

### Requirements

  * Available on all Helpdesk plans
  * The account owner and admins can access the API credentials and create API keys

## Find your API credentials

You can find the Base API URL (`https://{your-domain}.gorgias.com/api/`), Username (the email address on your account), and API key in your Gorgias settings. If you don’t have an existing API key, you’ll have to create one first.

# Connect your AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP

Updated October 26, 2026

### Who can use this feature?

 

All roles

 

All Helpdesk plans (AI Agent isn't required)

The Gorgias MCP lets you work with your Gorgias helpdesk using an AI assistant, like Claude or ChatGPT. Once you connect the MCP, your AI assistant can access your Gorgias data and account, so you can manage your helpdesk through conversations. For example, you can use an AI assistant to read and analyze your tickets, audit your account, configure AI Agent, and update your settings.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard that lets an AI tool connect to another app like Gorgias.

You can add the Gorgias MCP from Claude's connector directory or ChatGPT's plugin directory. If you use another AI client, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Copilot, you can create a custom connector for the MCP instead. This article covers:

  * Requirements
  * Who can use the Gorgias MCP?
  * Connecting an AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP

pages.text: Connect your AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP | Gorgias Help Center Ask anything Browse topics Get Started AI Agent & Automation Productivity Channels Integrations Account Setup Daily Operations Reporting & Analytics Resources Connect your AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP Updated October 26, 2026 On this page 8 sections Who can use this feature? All roles All Helpdesk plans (AI Agent isn't required) The Gorgias MCP lets you work with your Gorgias helpdesk using an AI assistant, like Claude or ChatGPT. Once you connect the MCP, your AI assistant can access your Gorgias data and account, so you can manage your helpdesk through conversations. For example, you can use an AI assistant to read and analyze your tickets, audit your account, configure AI Agent, and update your settings. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard that lets an AI tool connect to another app like Gorgias. You can add the Gorgias MCP from Claude's connector directory or ChatGPT's plugin directory. If you use another AI client, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Copilot, you can create a custom connector for the MCP instead. This article covers: Requirements Who can use the Gorgias MCP? Connecting an AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP Connecting Claude Connecting ChatGPT Authorizing your Gorgias account Connecting a different AI client, such as Claude Code What your AI assistant can do , with prompts to try Requirements A Gorgias account on any Helpdesk plan . An account with Claude, ChatGPT, or another MCP-compatible AI assistant. Your Gorgias subdomain. This is the your-brand part of your account URL ( your-brand.gorgias.com ). You'll enter it when you authorize the connection. Who can use the Gorgias MCP? Everyone can connect the Gorgias MCP, but the actions you can take with your AI assistant depend on the role assigned to your user in Gorgias. If your company uses Claude Team or Enterprise, or a managed ChatGPT workspace (Business, Enterprise, or Edu), an admin may need to make the Gorgias MCP available before you can connect. Connect an AI assistant to the Gorgias MCP Claude and ChatGPT both list the Gorgias MCP in their connector directories, so you can add it without any manual configuration. Follow the steps for the assistant you use, then authorize your Gorgias account to finish connecting. Connect Claude The Gorgias MCP is available in Claude's connector directory. You can connect the MCP using Claude on the web, desktop app, or mobile app. On Claude Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner or Primary Owner must enable the Gorgias MCP for your organization before members can connect it. Owners can find the steps in Claude's connector documentation . If you don't see the Gorgias MCP in your connectors list, ask your Owner to enable it. Note: Claude's menus change from time to time. For the most up-to-date steps, refer to Claude's connector documentation . In Claude, select Customize , then select Connectors . Browse the connector directory and search for Gorgias . Select Gorgias MCP , then select Connect . You're redirected to your browser. Authorize your Gorgias account . Connect ChatGPT The Gorgias MCP is available in ChatGPT as a plugin. If you use a managed ChatGPT workspace (Business, Enterprise, or Edu), an admin may need to make the Gorgias MCP available to your workspace first. Admins can find the steps in OpenAI's plugin controls documentation . If you can't find the Gorgias MCP in the directory, ask your workspace admin. Note: ChatGPT's menus change from time to time. For the most up-to-date steps, refer to OpenAI's plugin documentation . In ChatGPT, open the plugin directory and search for Gorgias MCP . Select Install plugin . Authorize your Gorgias account . Authorize your Gorgias account After you select Connect in Claude or Install plugin in ChatGPT, a browser window opens where you can authorize your AI assistant to connect with the Gorgias MCP. Enter your Gorgias subdomain (example: your-brand.gorgias.com ), then select Continue . Select Allow Access . Sign in to Gorgias. If you already have an active Gorgias session in your browser, you won't be prompted to sign in. Review the data the Gorgias MCP can access, then select Authorize . Return to Claude or ChatGPT. That's it. You're connected, and you can start prompting . Connect a different AI client Gorgias MCP works with any MCP-compatible AI client. The setup process varies by client, but the connection URL is the same: https://mcp.gorgias.com/mcp Refer to your AI client's documentation for how to add an HTTP MCP server, then complete the Gorgias authentication step when prompted: Claude Code (if you sign in with your Claude account, connectors you add in Claude on the web are also available in Claude Code) Codex Cursor VS Code Copilot What your AI assistant can do Once connected, your AI assistant can read your helpdesk data and take actions on your behalf, within the limits of your Gorgias role . It can work with: Tickets: search and read tickets, reply to customers, add internal notes, and update status, priority, and assignee, and add tags. pages.title: Access your Gorgias REST API credentials (https://docs.gorgias.com/en-US/rest-api-208286)
pages.text: Access your Gorgias REST API credentials Search All articles Access your Gorgias REST API credentials Updated 5 months ago The Gorgias REST API lets you read and write data in your helpdesk programmatically. To authenticate API requests, Gorgias uses HTTP Basic Authentication with three pieces of information: your base API URL, your email address, and an API key. You can find and manage all three from the REST API settings page in your helpdesk. Note: API keys are tied to your individual account, not to the helpdesk as a whole. For full API documentation, visit the Gorgias Developer Documentation . Requirements Available on all Helpdesk plans The account owner and admins can access the API credentials and create API keys Find your API credentials You can find the Base API URL ( https://{your-domain}.gorgias.com/api/ ), Username (the email address on your account), and API key in your Gorgias settings. If you don’t have an existing API key, you’ll have to create one first. From your helpdesk, click the Settings icon in the bottom-left corner. In the menu, locate Account , then select REST API . Under API Access & Credentials , you'll find the Base API URL , your Username , and Password (API Key) . Click Copy next to any field to copy it to your clipboard. Create an API key If you haven't created an API key yet, the Password field will show a Create API key button instead of a key value. From your helpdesk, click the Settings icon in the bottom-left corner. In the menu, locate Account , then select REST API . Under Password (API Key) , click Create API Key . Your API key is generated immediately and displayed alongside the other credentials. Your API key grants full access to your account's data. Once you’ve copied it, store it somewhere secure and don’t share it with anyone. Reset your API key You can reset your API key at any time. Resetting generates a new key and immediately invalidates the old one. Any integrations or scripts using the old key will stop working until they're updated with the new one. From your helpdesk, click the Settings icon in the bottom-left corner. In the menu, locate Account , then select REST API . Next to the Password (API Key) field, click Reset . Click OK to confirm. Import the Postman collection The REST API settings page also includes a Run in Postman button. Clicking it imports the Gorgias Postman collection with your domain, email address, and API key pre-filled as environment variables, so you can start making requests immediately.
